newsitem.title: FRANCE: France meets EMU criteria, to cut spending - Juppe.
newsitem.headline: France meets EMU criteria, to cut spending - Juppe.

text.p: France meets the Maastricht criteria for joining the euro single currency, but still needs extra spending cuts, Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Sunday.
"We are within the (Maastricht) criteria. What's more, the Brussels (European) Commission has said that France qualifies or pre-qualifies," he said in an interview on TF1 television.
"We are within forecasts and everybody considers that we are not far off," he said. But he added, "Extra measures are needed, it is true, which is why I say we must not increase public spending."
Juppe said the extra spending cuts did not constitute further austerity, in the way that the public felt the effect of tax increases imposed by the government since election in 1995.
That first stage of mastering public finances was over. But the government would limit future spending below the rate of inflation over the next five years, he said.
"Controlling public spending is an absolute necessity. That is why you cannot talk about austerity. Not raising spending at an excessive rate is not austerity, it is wisdom," he said.
Excessive spending had to be paid for out of taxation whereas the government aimed to press ahead with tax cuts in the future, if sufficient growth allowed, he said.
The European Commission reported on Wednesday that France looked likely to contain its public deficit to three percent of gross domestic product, a key requirement for joining the euro in 1999.
